 Remarks at One Earth Summit 2026
 Speeches
 28 Oct 2026
 Remarks at One Earth Summit 2026
 Arthur Yuen, Deputy Chief Executive, Hong Kong Monetary Authority
 Connecting Sustainable Finance with Climate-Resilient Growth 
 Introduction
 Good afternoon everyone. To those who have travelled from overseas to join us today, welcome to Hong Kong.
 Not sure if some of you have come here today through Tuen Mun, by the tunnel that runs under the water to the bridge port and the airport. Take a moment to think about that name, Tuen Mun. It appears in Tang-dynasty records, more than a thousand years ago. It was a garrison post at a gateway, watching over the merchants and travellers, Chinese and foreign, who passed through. Some historians described it as a node of the maritime Silk Road. So, if you did take the route from Tuen Mun to come here, you were actually following a very old route that had been used by traders. 
 This little story tells us that Hong Kong has been a meeting point for trade for a very long time. The legacy of leveraging our advantages to serve as a gateway remains deeply embedded in our roots today. But there is a key difference: Hong Kong has now evolved far beyond a trading hub. 
 Today, Hong Kong positions ourselves as a super-connector and home to hubs of many kinds. The HKSAR Government’s inaugural Five-Year Plan, which seeks to consolidate and enhance the “Four Centres and One Hub”, underscores our versatility and capacity to act as a focal point across multiple dimensions. We seamlessly bridge Hong Kong, Chinese Mainland, and Asia with the global market; connect financing needs with international capital; bridge technological ideas with practical applications, and talents across boundaries.
 To remain an effective connector and hub, we have to stay attuned to the evolving global landscape. Geopolitical, technological and economic developments have dominated the headlines. But sustainability—and climate change in particular—has also become a defining priority. We all have witnessed, and probably felt firsthand, the growing frequency and heightening impact of extreme weather events across the globe. Climate change is a universal challenge. It spares no jurisdiction and no economy.
 Action is needed and so is capital. Mitigation requires three to four times the current global finance flows. Adaptation in developing countries requires 12 to 14 times current international public finance flows.
 As an international financial hub, Hong Kong has both a responsibility and an opportunity to connect sustainable capital with the pressing needs. The HKMA is fully committed to advancing this agenda, as set out in the Sustainable Finance Action Agenda launched in 2024.
 Hong Kong as an international sustainable hub
 Hong Kong has led Asia’s league table for arranging international green and sustainable bonds in Asia for eight consecutive years. The momentum is encouraging but more can be, and has to be done. 
 We are strengthening Hong Kong as an international sustainable finance hub along two dimensions: depth and breadth. We are deepening its foundations through common standards, greater awareness and higher transparency. At the same time, we are extending its reach by bringing together capital, people and technology.
 Deepening the foundation
 Let me begin with the foundation. A hub needs a common language and a trusted standard. They build confidence in the market and give participants a clear basis on which to act. In sustainable finance, this means answers to some fundamental questions. What would be green enough to be labelled green? What is transition considering the sectoral development? What is adaptation given the local context?

 部分媒體報導楊總裁對主權基金議題之看法，與事實不符 
 一、今(28)日部分媒體報導本行總裁赴立法院財委會答覆立委有關成立主權基金之質詢時，「強調主權基金不應動用外匯存底，畢竟外匯存底具有穩定經濟的特定法定職責」，此報導與事實不符。
 二、楊總裁答詢時僅表示，主要先進國家多有在推動主權基金，台灣有這個經濟實力可以設立主權基金，從未提及主權基金不應動用外匯存底。

FED'S WARSH: ASKED IF MIDTERM ELECTIONS FACTORED INTO RATE DECISION, SAYS POLITICS PLAYED NO ROLE
FED CHAIR WARSH SAYS CREDIT SPREADS HAVE WIDENED FOR SOME ASSETS, WITH SOME TIGHTENING IN SOME FINANCIAL CONDITIONS
FED CHAIR WARSH SAYS INTEREST RATES DO MATTER FOR NEW TECHNOLOGY, THAT CAPEX IS BROADENING, AND THAT THE STRENGTH IN CAPEX IS NO LONGER IN NARROW POCKETS
FED CHAIR WARSH, ASKED IF THE MIDTERM ELECTIONS FACTORED INTO THE RATE DECISION, SAYS POLITICS PLAYED NO ROLE AND THAT HE DID NOT HEAR ANY REFERENCE TO POLITICS OR ELECTIONS IN FOMC DELIBERATIONS
FED CHAIR WARSH SAYS POLITICS DID NOT HAVE ANY ROLE, NOT JUST FOR HIM BUT FOR HIS COLLEAGUES, AND THAT THE COMING PERIOD WILL BE INFORMATION-RICH BUT HAS NOTHING TO DO WITH POLITICS
FED CHAIR WARSH SAYS HE DOES NOT BELIEVE IN FORWARD GUIDANCE ABSENT A CRISIS, AND DOES NOT BELIEVE IN PREJUDGING MEETINGS
FED CHAIR WARSH SAYS HE WON’T SHARE MUSINGS ON WHAT WILL HAPPEN IN DECEMBER, ADDING THAT THE FED MIGHT LEARN A LOT BY THEN AND WILL BE BETTER-POSITIONED TO DETERMINE THE RIGHT POLICY DECISION
FED CHAIR WARSH SAYS HE PAYS A LOT OF ATTENTION TO THE KOREAN ECONOMY, WHICH TELLS HIM WHAT IS COMING THIS WAY
FED CHAIR WARSH SAYS HE IS GLAD THE KOREAN CENTRAL BANK GOVERNOR IS IN HIS POST, THAT HE HAS KNOWN HIM FOR 20 YEARS AND THAT HE IS A GOOD FRIEND

FED CHAIR WARSH SAYS THE BALANCE SHEET TASK FORCE RECOMMENDATIONS WILL BE FED INTO THE FOMC EARLY IN THE FIRST QUARTER, AND THAT IF THE FED DECIDES TO MAKE BALANCE SHEET CHANGES, IT IS UNLIKELY TO HAVE ANY EFFECT ON THIS POLICY JUNCTURE

FED CHAIR WARSH SAYS ANY CHANGES TO THE BALANCE SHEET WILL COME AFTER SERIOUS CONSIDERATION OF THE TASK FORCE RECOMMENDATIONS, AND THAT WHEN THE FED REMOVED A DOSE OF ACCOMMODATION, THE EFFECTS ON FINANCIAL MARKET CONDITIONS WERE CONSISTENT WITH EXPECTATIONS
FED'S WARSH: IS ECONOMY RUNNING TOO HOT? THAT IS NOT JUDGMENT OF MOST OF MY COLLEAGUES
FED CHAIR WARSH SAYS THE FED’S MEASURES OF THE SIZE OF THE AGGREGATE DEMAND CURVE ARE IMPERFECT, BUT THAT THE ECONOMY IS STRONG AND POINTING IN THE RIGHT DIRECTION
FED CHAIR WARSH, ASKED WHETHER THE ECONOMY IS RUNNING TOO HOT, SAYS THAT IS NOT THE JUDGMENT OF MOST OF HIS COLLEAGUES, ADDING THAT PRODUCTIVITY HAS BEEN MOVING HIGHER

FED CHAIR WARSH SAYS ECONOMIC GROWTH IS HIGHER, BUT THAT DOES NOT MEAN IT IS CAUSING INFLATION, AND THAT THE GOAL IS NOT TO THROW SAND INTO THE GEARS OF THE ECONOMY, ADDING HE DOES NOT THINK THE FED HAS TO THROW PEOPLE OUT OF WORK
FED CHAIR WARSH SAYS THE FED IS TIGHTENING FINANCIAL CONDITIONS, THAT THIS TELLS HIM POLICY IS WORKING, AND THAT HE IS NOT UNCOMFORTABLE WITH IT
